label: prop:h3-frobenius-casimir-markov-trace
title: Frobenius Casimir of $H_3(q)$: Schur elements, Markov weights, its Markov trace, and $\sum_{\lambda\vdash3}1/\dim_q\lambda = 2+1/[2]_q$
html:
Let K be a field and q\in K^\times with q^2+1\ne0 and q^4+q^2+1\ne0. Let H_3=H_3(K,q) have generators \sigma_1,\sigma_2 with \sigma_i^2=(q-q^{-1})\sigma_i+1 and standard basis \{T_w\}_{w\in S_3}. Write h=q-q^{-1}, [2]_q=q+q^{-1}, and let \kappa(\lambda) be the content sum of \lambda. The canonical symmetrising form is \tau_0(T_w)=\delta_{w,1}, with dual basis T_w^\vee=T_{w^{-1}}. Its Frobenius Casimir is C_{\mathrm{Frob}}:=\sum_{w\in S_3}T_wT_{w^{-1}}. For z\in K, \mathrm{tr}^z is the Ocneanu trace (\mathrm{tr}^z(1)=1, \mathrm{tr}^z(x\sigma_2)=z\,\mathrm{tr}^z(x) for x\in H_2), and write z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1) for the two-row Markov parameter. Then:

  1. (Casimir.) C_{\mathrm{Frob}} = 6+3h(T_{s_1}+T_{s_2})+h^2(T_{s_1s_2}+T_{s_2s_1})+(q^3-q^{-3})T_{w_0}. It is central and acts on the block \lambda by c_\lambda d_\lambda, where d_\lambda is the block dimension and the Schur elements of \tau_0 are c_\lambda = q^{\kappa(\lambda)}\prod_{x\in\lambda}[h_x]_q: c_{(3)}=q^3[3]_q!, c_{(2,1)}=[3]_q, c_{(1^3)}=q^{-3}[3]_q!.
  2. (Markov weights.) \mathrm{tr}^z=\sum_\lambda y_\lambda(z)\chi_\lambda with
y_{(3)}=\frac{(qz+1)(q^3z+qz+1)}{(q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)},\qquad
y_{(2,1)}=\frac{q(q-z)(qz+1)}{q^4+q^2+1},\qquad
y_{(1^3)}=\frac{q^2(z-q)(q^2z+z-q^3)}{(q^2+1)(q^4+q^2+1)}.

At z = z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1): y_{(3)}=(q^4+1)/(q^2+1)^2, y_{(2,1)}=1/[2]_q^2 and y_{(1^3)}=0. 3. (Trace of the Casimir.)

\mathrm{tr}^z(C_{\mathrm{Frob}}) = 6+6hz+2h^2z^2+(q^3-q^{-3})(hz^2+z),

and at z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1)

\mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})=\frac{(q^4+q^2+1)(q^6+q^4+q^2+5)}{(q^2+1)^2},
\mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})-\Bigl(2+\frac1{[2]_q}\Bigr)=\frac{q^{10}+2q^8+3q^6+5q^4-q^3+2q^2-q+3}{(q^2+1)^2}.

In particular \mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(C_{\mathrm{Frob}})\ne 2+1/[2]_q as rational functions of q (at q=1 the two sides are 6 and 5/2). 4. (Inverse q-dimension sum.) With \dim_q\lambda=[3]_q!/\prod_{x\in\lambda}[h_x]_q,

\sum_{\lambda\vdash 3}\frac{1}{\dim_q\lambda} = \frac{1}{[3]_q!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash3}q^{-\kappa(\lambda)}c_\lambda = 2+\frac{1}{[2]_q},

and over the blocks on which \mathrm{tr}^{z_0} is nonzero the sum is 1+1/[2]_q=(q^2+q+1)/(q^2+1). 5. (The element C_{\dim_q} is not the Frobenius Casimir.) For any trace t on H_3 with t(e_\lambda)\ne0 for all \lambda, the central element C_{\dim_q}=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda/(\dim_q(\lambda)\,t(e_\lambda)) of Universal Frobenius co-dimension trace: \tau(C_{\dim_q}) = \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q(\lambda) has t(C_{\dim_q})=\sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda by construction. At z_0 = q^3/(q^2+1) it is undefined, because \mathrm{tr}^{z_0}(e_{(1^3)})=0.

Two inputs are cited rather than proved here: that C_{\mathrm{Frob}} acts on block \lambda by the scalar c_\lambda d_\lambda in item 1, of which only the implied trace identity is established, and the associativity of the six-dimensional matrix model of H_3 used to compute in it.

So the identity \sum_\lambda 1/\dim_q\lambda=2+1/[2]_q is a formal sum (item 4), and it is not the Markov trace of the Frobenius Casimir (item 3).
